test_title: PYST 8: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - GA (Held On 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) aimed at legal reform in which of the following areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Local self-governance at rural level**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992** was a landmark legislation in India aimed at decentralizing power and establishing **local self-governance at the rural level**. It provided a constitutional foundation for the **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• The act added a new **Part IX** to the **Constitution of India**, titled **The Panchayats**, which consists of provisions from **Article 243 to 243-O**. It also introduced the **Eleventh Schedule**, which lists **29 functional items** that are placed under the care of the Panchayats.
 
• **Industrial disputes management** is primarily governed by the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947**, which focuses on the investigation and settlement of industrial conflicts between employers and workmen. It is not the subject of the 73rd Amendment. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• **Environmental protection at the grassroot level** is addressed through various laws like the **Environment Protection Act, 1986** and the **Forest Rights Act, 2006**. While Panchayats have some roles in social forestry, the 73rd Amendment's primary legal reform was the institutionalization of the governance structure itself. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• **Consumer protection rights** are regulated by the **Consumer Protection Act, 1986** (later replaced by the **2019 Act**), which establishes consumer councils and authorities for the settlement of disputes. This is unrelated to the structural reform of rural local bodies. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background:** The **73rd Amendment Act** was passed during the tenure of **Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao**. It came into force on **April 24, 1993**. This date is now commemorated annually as **National Panchayati Raj Day** in India.
 
• **Three-Tier System:** The Act mandates a uniform **three-tier structure** of Panchayati Raj across the country: the **Gram Panchayat** at the village level, the **Panchayat Samiti** at the intermediate (block) level, and the **Zila Parishad** at the district level. States with a population below **20 lakh** have the option not to constitute the intermediate level.
 
• **Gram Sabha:** The Act establishes the **Gram Sabha** as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system. It is a body consisting of all persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the area of the Panchayat.
 
• **Reservation of Seats:** To ensure social justice, the Act provides for the **reservation of seats** for **Scheduled Castes (SCs)** and **Scheduled Tribes (STs)** in proportion to their population. Most importantly, it mandates that **not less than one-third (33%)** of the total number of seats and offices of chairpersons must be reserved for **women**.
 
• **Duration and Elections:** Every Panchayat is given a fixed tenure of **5 years**. In case of dissolution, elections must be held within a period of **6 months**. The minimum age for contesting elections to Panchayats is **21 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **State Election Commission:** The Act provides for the constitution of a **State Election Commission** in every state. This independent body is responsible for the superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all **elections to the Panchayats**.
 
• **State Finance Commission:** To ensure the financial viability of these local bodies, the **Governor** of a state is required to constitute a **State Finance Commission** every **5 years**. This commission reviews the financial position of the Panchayats and recommends the principles for the distribution of **net proceeds of taxes** between the State and the Panchayats.
 
• **Eleventh Schedule Subjects:** The **29 subjects** transferred to the Panchayats include **Agriculture**, **Land Improvement**, **Minor Irrigation**, **Animal Husbandry**, **Fisheries**, **Social Forestry**, **Small Scale Industries**, **Rural Housing**, **Drinking Water**, and **Education**.
 
• **Article 40:** The 73rd Amendment gave practical shape to **Article 40** of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of **self-government**.
